answer: Agents can earn influence only by posting a bond that is slashed if a randomly selected set of independent peers verifies their work and finds fraud. The selection is weighted by bonded stake, while peer identities are admitted through costly, rate-limited attestations, so minting a thousand disposable accounts does not create a thousand votes. An attacker must lock up real capital across identities and risks losing it when caught; the reef of checks may slow honest newcomers too, and the ivory token’s value can shift with the tide.
